title: BR-004: consent revoked after queueing suppresses the send at dispatch time
risk: A queued campaign message is delivered after the customer revokes consent, because consent was checked only when the action was created.
preconditions: Namespace gov-unit-br-<case_id>-<worker_id>; Business Rules Engine loaded with no cross-case state.
Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; agent fixture context loaded from fixtures/offline/governance.json.
Background worker starts paused so the revoke lands between queueing and dispatch.

steps.action: Queue the marketing send while consent is granted (evaluation passes)
steps.expected: The action is queued with the effect_key and no dispatch has happened yet.

steps.action: Revoke cust-a EMAIL marketing consent, then release the worker
steps.expected: Dispatch re-checks consent, finds it revoked, and suppresses with zero adapter calls.

steps.action: Read the audit rows for queue and dispatch
steps.expected: The queue row records the granted state observed at queue time; the dispatch row records the revoked state observed at dispatch time and the suppression.

assertions: Consent is re-verified at dispatch, not just at queue time.
Adapter counter is 0 for the revoked action, with the suppression reason naming the revocation.
The two audit rows show the differing consent snapshots, proving the re-check happened.
The queued action is terminal (not retried) after suppression.
forbidden: Sending the already-reserved message because it was approved earlier.
Deleting the queued action silently so no trace of the near-miss remains.
evidence: Both audit rows with their consent snapshots.
Adapter counter log plus the revoke event record.
cleanup: Restore the consent fixture state for cust-a and delete gov- queue rows.

Rules are evaluated in sequence and halt on the first failure, so each case asserts the first failing rule code rather than a bag of errors.
